name: Cameo Brown
lede: Cameo Brown is a muted reddish brown from Ridgway's 1912 plates, filed by the ISCC-NBS dictionary under grayish red rather than brown.

sections.title: Named brown, classed as red
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature plates it at plate XXVIII, hue 7'', tone k, hex #886153 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary also carries the name, on its own plate 6 F 9, dated 1912 [1]. The ISCC-NBS committee filed it in 1955 under block 19, grayish red, though the swatch sits a loose 7.4 units from that block's center [1]. The named brown is classed with the reds [1]. Its Munsell renotation is 1.9YR 4.4/3.5 [1]. The name's own origin is undocumented here [1].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[prussian-red|Prussian Red]], 3.4 units away, a coincidence of hue and not a shared history with the pigment Prussian blue; [[sandalwood|Sandalwood]] follows at 3.7 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within six units of Cameo Brown covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 834 of 23,781 paintings, about 3.5 per cent, as photographed [2]. Its earliest appearance is a Roman-era carved stone fragment, *Griffin Atop Entablature*, dated to around year 1, where it covers five per cent of the surface [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1270s, and Pontormo and the Danish painter Niels Skovgaard carry it well above the archive average [2]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, read as screen colors [2].
